body: **2026-10-06-telemetry-bootstrap** — (§3 obs log format) measured escher's sink as non-JSON stderr lines behind the allowlist scrub (`text`/`value`/`html`/`attrs` redacted, only safe fields for `blitz*`/`accesskit_xplat`); this chunk's "scrub held" boundary is that sink, and no a11y violation schema is defined against it, so a captured record entering an answer must not reshape it.

**2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist** — the sink gained its third outcome: records from a target outside `escher_*`/`blitz*`/`accesskit_xplat` are dropped whole at every level; a per-step capture layer must see what the sink drops versus prints, and an app handler's own log under an app target is exactly such a dropped record today.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** — restated the sink as two record classes (events, and one line per closed span of an admitted target) and added `tracing` as escher-driver's dependency; the scope forbids the `command` span gaining any field carrying the new answer content, and this is the span class that would print it.

**2026-10-09-founder-rulings** — the closed-span record class ratified by the founder (2026-10-09); one of the "log rulings of 2026-10-07/09" that bound the founder's boundary fork on what of a log may enter an answer.

**2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — every Dioxus element node carries its stable id as `author_id` (row `contract/accessibility-tree/author-id`) and the tree is built through `Document::accessibility_tree` (rows `decision/accessibility-tree-through-document-method`, `decision/a11y-tree-through-document-trait`); the stable element id this chunk ties each error to is that identity, never a `NodeId`.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — the snapshot reads role, name and focus from the tree with no second mapping (origin of `decision/snapshot-model-single-source`, `decision/readers-of-one-snapshot-model`); the new answer field sits beside the diff and must not become a second source of role or name.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — the actionable-key rule (`decision/actionable-key-rule`, guard `unkeyed_actionable`): every actionable element reads an author key; trap: never satisfy the check by adding a `tabindex` or role. A fixture app beside the stand that panics or logs from a handler must key its elements so the error ties to a stable id.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — a password input reads `MASKED_VALUE` (origin of `decision/password-value-masked`); a captured panic payload or log field must never carry typed text a mask hides elsewhere.

**2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization** — `Snapshot::to_text` added as a reader of the model, and a file input's path masked; precedent that each new answer form reads the model alone and that path-like text is kept out of every field.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — the tree refreshes on a poll whose drained changed set was non-empty (`decision/a11y-tree-refresh-on-change`) and the diff an acting call returns reads the snapshot model; the new field rides beside that diff and must not alter the changed-set drain.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — the refresh on change and its changed-set contract ratified by the founder (2026-10-07); a caught panic leaving the instance held must keep the changed set and refresh semantics this ruling fixed.

**2026-10-07-settle-detection** — a harness settle (`Harness::settle`, the session's `act`) neither reads nor drains the changed set, and a fresh boot holds a non-empty set (`decision/harness-settle-leaves-changed-set`, guard `stand_settle`); trap for a per-step capture around the run path: do not drain the set, and drain first in a check that reads it as one step's change.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — the driver's schema defines no role or name set (`decision/driver-schema-has-no-role-set`); a new result field enters only as the schema tables admit, as the scope requires.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — escher-driver names `accessibility` on dioxus-native-dom unconditionally, so both seven_guis binaries compile the gated readers; the graph reader the error-to-handler tie needs is reachable from the driver for that reason, while no stand binary builds an adapter.

**2026-10-07-refusal-detection** — `Session::run` refuses `click`/`type` on `enabled == Some(false)` with nothing dispatched, the first of its screen-level checks; a refused step dispatches no handler, so it can cause no handler error to report.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — an MCP result is a reader of the snapshot model only; an acting call's result is its JSON line with the diff (`contract/mcp-result/snapshot`), the crossing ratified by the founder 2026-10-10; the new field on MCP extends this line and his field rule of 2026-10-10 judges whether it is a widening.

**2026-10-12-self-description** — the password over MCP reads `MASKED_VALUE`, sentinel 0 times, and `help` (the node keys' help) became a closed-words reader of the model; the scope's `help` and MCP listing describing the new field follow this precedent, and a sentinel-count check is the pattern for proving no typed text crosses.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — a password's text in no painted frame either (`decision/password-never-revealed`), the founder's fork 2; extends the no-typed-text boundary the error field must respect on every carrier.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** — (§5, §6: `inert` and `disabled`) a disabled form control takes neither activation key, a `disabled` on a `summary` or `a` gating neither; ratified 2026-10-18 (Epoch 2 close entry); bounds which keyboard steps reach a handler.

**2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts** — an MCP `snapshot` result is the text for a whole screen and a `{text, part, parts}` JSON line for a paged one (`contract/mcp-result/snapshot`); an answer that grows by captured records must stay within the answer forms and budgets this set.

**2026-10-24-a11y-re-read** — the `a11y` leg runs fourteen files by the founder's word, each joining file a witness or a tree reading he took; a new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/` target for this chunk joins no a11y leg list unless so ruled.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** — (the scrollbar's band) right after a `scroll` a driver click in the shown overlay scrollbar band is a thumb drag and dispatches nothing (`decision/driver-click-in-shown-scrollbar-drags`); such a step reaches no handler and must report no handler error.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** — (the `MountedData` hazard in a spawned task) a `MountedData` call in a task spawned from a key handler panicked `RefCell already borrowed`; the stand's one recorded handler panic, the class of panic this chunk would now catch and return.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** — (the driver on a `multiple` select) `type` focuses a select with no click and the driver's closed sets of verbs, arguments, key names, result fields, causes, session errors and exits gain nothing (`decision/driver-type-focuses-select-no-click`); the scope's "no new verb, exit status or session error" rests on those same closed sets.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — (the driver's `type` on any select) `type` widened from a `multiple` select to any select, closing any list, firing no DOM focus events; the current form of `decision/driver-type-focuses-select-no-click`.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — (how an open list's labels leave) an option's and a group's label leave only as screenshot pixels and the snapshot's `name`, "with no log site", ratified by the founder (`decision/option-labels-leave-only-as-pixels`); a captured log record entering an answer must not open a new route for page text.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — (what the snapshot and an AT read of an open list) no `expanded` node key, `NODE_FIELDS` thirteen (`absence/snapshot-list-open-state`), a row's own `bounds` read as a closed set by the field rule of 2026-10-10; the same rule judges whether the new answer field is a widening.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — (an open list has no motion) motion on an open list observed absent, a screen read after a step needing no `advance` (`absence/select-list-motion`); an error captured on a step is read in that step's answer with no `advance`.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** — (a key press past a dropped anonymous block) a key-press panic in the engine fixed as escher's own, with a check outside both a11y and stand-repeat legs; precedent that an engine panic is fixed, not caught, while this chunk catches only the app handler's panic.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** — (the listener mark's over-report) the `data-dioxus-id` mark and event attributes over-report removed listeners while the vdom walk's dynamic attributes read current listeners exactly; tie a handler error to the handler through the exact listener reading, never the mark.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** — (the MountedData hazard re-measured) the panic is `DioxusDocument::poll` holding `inner.borrow_mut()` across `render_immediate`, pinned by `should_panic` pins in `dioxus_runtime_probe`; the measured site where a panic arises on the poll and run path.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** — (the probe target outside the a11y leg) `dioxus_runtime_probe` joined no `a11y` or `stand-repeat` leg and is reached by the workspace `test` leg and `run`; placement precedent for this chunk's new blitz-tests target and fixture.

**2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** — (the spawned-task MountedData hazard record, closed by the buffered render) the panic retired by rendering into a `MutationBuffer` unborrowed; the two `should_panic` pins became acting pins. A panic fixture must not lean on that retired panic.

**2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** — (the buffered render's same-render limit) a task polled during a render acts on the document as the previous render left it; an error from such a task is attributed against that state, a limit owned by an open residual row.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** — (the read-only UI graph reader `DioxusDocument::graph`) one node per snapshot node; ids, component, state and handler event names, closed flag words and booleans, never a value; no served id holds `///` (`decision/ui-graph-one-node-per-snapshot-node`, `decision/ui-graph-carries-no-values`, `contract/node-id/reserved-separator`); the handler identity (owner id and event name) this chunk ties errors to, and its no-value rule.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** — (graph state registration and the bridge dispatch's write record) where a `SignalRegistry` is registered, `DioxusEventHandler::handle_event` sets the dispatch (chain and event) around `runtime.handle_event` and clears it after; the natural seam, and a trap, for attributing a step's panic or log to its handler, since a panic must not leave the dispatch set.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** — (the «reacts to a click» snapshot field built as `NodeState.clickable`) `NODE_FIELDS` 13 → 14 and `Reading::ALL` 11 → 12, read from current listeners; a precedent for how a new answer or snapshot field grows the closed field tables and the `help` text.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** — (the one actionable rule and the check's listener leg) `unkeyed_actionable` and `actionable_nodes` share the crate-private `Readings`, its listener leg the exact current listeners other than `mounted`, the mark serving event dispatch alone (`decision/one-actionable-rule`).

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** — (the actionable-node reader) `actionable_nodes` added behind `accessibility`, beside the ungated `signal_registry` (`decision/agent-readers-behind-accessibility`); the wasm build compiles dioxus-native-dom without that feature, so any capture on the dispatch path must decide its gate.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** — (the actions verb as a read-only reader) the `actions` answer writes ids, owner ids, verb and cause words and booleans only, never a value, typed text, `MASKED_VALUE` or `NodeId` (`contract/actions-answer/fields`), its crossing on every carrier the founder's word; the template for the error field's closed content and the founder's fork if authored text crosses.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** — (the keyed reading, provisional on the carriers) a new field on the carriers stood PROVISIONAL as a delegate's call until the founder's word; how a new answer field is marked when the founder is away, as now.
**2026-11-13T07-43-19-wrap** — `~ decision/keyed-wire-form` provisional → standing on the founder's «Утвердить keyed»; the closing step of the keyed precedent.

**2026-11-08-handler-coverage** — (the ungated reached record on `handle_event`'s path) `record_reached`/`reached_handlers` record (id, event) per dispatch before `runtime.handle_event`, ungated, a removed element still counting, one `has_context` lookup per dispatch elsewhere (`contract/dioxus-document/reached-handlers`, `contract/dioxus-document/record-reached`); one of the scope's named candidates for attributing an error to a handler.

**2026-11-08-handler-coverage** — (`stand_handler_coverage`'s keyboard-activation check) a refused step exercises nothing and a keyboard activation its control's click, in both modes, in `stand-repeat` by prefix and no a11y leg list; the same refused and keyboard cases bound what errors a step can carry.

**2026-11-08-handler-coverage** — (`handler_coverage`, a further reader of the UI graph) reads the graph at boot and after each replayed step, `mounted` left out, answer of ids, owner ids, event names and two counts only (`contract/handler-coverage/answer`); the kept-check replay path the new field must also ride.

Each item is tied to the stable element id the step acted on and, through the UI graph, to the handler that ran (owner id and event name) — the graph's existing node identity, never an engine node id.
A handler panic during a step on a held session is caught on the run path and returned as the call's outcome instead of ending the host process; records emitted during a step are captured, bounded per call.
The field rides every ratified carrier of the acting verbs (in process, the session socket's call, the command line, MCP, the kept check recorded and replayed), and the driver's help and the MCP tool listing describe it.
What of a log may enter an answer is the founder's boundary fork; the telemetry scrub, the span fields and the log lines stay as they are.

body: The acting verbs' answer gains one field listing the handler panic, error-level log record or handler log record the step caused; the snapshot diff it returns today stays beside it unchanged.

Each item of the new field is tied to the served node id of the element the step acted on and, through the UI graph, to the handler that ran (owner id and event name) — the UI graph's existing node identity and the reached-handler record, never an engine node id.

A handler panic during a step on a held session is caught on the run path and returned as the call's outcome rather than ending the host process; what the instance is after a caught panic is read in P3.
The capture of what a step caused: records emitted during the step, bounded per call, attributed to the step's target and handler.
The same field on every ratified carrier the acting verbs ride: in process, the session socket's call, the command line, the MCP tool results and the kept check, recorded and replayed.
The driver's self-description and the MCP tool listing describe the new field.

Indirect, through the carriers: any authored text crossing onto a carrier — a panic payload, a log message, a log field's value — is a boundary widening the founder decides; a new field of a closed value set inside a ratified carrier is not one. The founder's log rulings bound it: content-free log fields, no screen content in logs, the closed-span line.

Indirect, through the telemetry sink: the target allowlist and the redaction of escher targets' fields stay as they are; the driver's command span and the MCP tool_call span gain no field holding what the answer now carries; no log line carries the new answer content.
Indirect, through the answer: a password value is never revealed and no screen content leaves through the new field — a captured record's text is subject to the same rule as any answer value.
No new carrier, listener, socket, port, verb, exit status or session error; a new refusal cause or result field only as the driver schema's tables admit and the plan names.
No panic path on a driver call's arguments: a panic caught here is the app handler's, never the driver's.
The UI graph stays read-only and carries no values: the handler identity is read from it, and nothing captured is written into it.
The layout read, explore and Session::reach keep their contracts; explore's per-path panic ending is not widened to carry a payload.

Whether the new field joins the kept answer's comparison as any other answer field or is held out of the digest is a design point for P4; the kept check's recording and replay must stay deterministic either way.
The proof: a minimal fixture app beside the stand whose handlers panic, return an error and log, driven through every acting verb, in a new test target run in both layout modes.

Key handling contracts of controls — range input keys, single and multiple select keys and lists, the Cells grid, the CRUD list, Tab order, keyboard activation: the acting verbs keep what they do to a control; only their answer gains a field.

**2026-10-06-telemetry-bootstrap** — registered escher-telemetry: `init` / `init_with_writer`, the stderr line, the allowlist scrub (`CONTENT_FIELDS` redacted), the panic event at `escher_telemetry::panic` with a redacted `panic.payload` and a chaining panic hook; matters because this chunk must capture a step's records and a handler panic without changing what the sink prints (scope «Scrub held»), and the panic hook already redacts the payload this chunk would carry into an answer.

**2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist** — the sink admits only `ENGINE_TARGET_PREFIXES` and `ESCHER_TARGET_PREFIXES` (`escher_`), an engine target printing `SAFE_FIELDS` only, an escher target every field but `CONTENT_FIELDS`, any other target dropped whole at every level in the formatter; standing rule that a new escher log target must start with `escher_`. A per-step capture layer must not move this drop/scrub (rows decision/telemetry-target-prefix-drop, contract/telemetry-scrub/*), and an app's handler log under its own target is dropped by the sink today, a fact the capture design must reckon with.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** (the command span; `tracing` its third dependency) — every call through `Session::run` opens one hand-built `command` span (target `escher_driver`, INFO, eight fields, never an argument, `Outcome`, `Refusal`, screen text); the crate installs no subscriber and reads no env var; `stand_act_spans` re-executes children installing the sink over an in-memory capture. Matters: the scope holds that `command` / `tool_call` gain no field carrying the new answer content (decision/driver-spans-only, contract/command-span/never-fielded, decision/driver-library-side-effect-free), and the re-exec + in-memory capture is the precedent for proving a capture without a global subscriber in the driver.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** (the sink prints a closed span; the diff's lengths reach a log — both PROVISIONAL) — added the sink's closed-span line and the diff's three counts on the command span; these are the founder's «log rulings of 2026-10-07/09» the scope says bound what of a log may enter an answer (decision/telemetry-closed-span-lines, decision/diff-content-never-logged).

**2026-10-09-founder-rulings** — ratified the closed-span line and the diff counts in a log, with the standing rule «a count of a diff's nodes may reach a log, nothing of its content may», and the ruling that an in-process call returning screen content is the returned value his rule allows. This is the 2026-10-09 log ruling the chunk's boundary fork is bounded by: the reverse direction (log content into an answer) is the new question for the founder.

**2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization** — the snapshot text left the process through the returned value only, with the standing rule that each later surface asks the crossing question again when content first leaves the process; precedent for treating authored log/panic text entering an answer as a crossing to put to the founder (decision/snapshot-text-never-logged, decision/no-snapshot-in-logs).

**2026-10-07-settle-detection** — `Harness::settle`, `Session::act` and `NotSettled(Busy)`: a not-settled step is a result, not rolled back, its outcome naming a class only; settle logs nothing. Matters: a caught handler panic or captured error is likewise a result field on the acting step, not a refusal or session error (contract/acting-verb-results/settled), and the settle path must stay silent.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — one `VERBS` table every surface reads, the acting result fields `settled` · `busy` · `added` · `removed` · `changed`, causes closed at eight, rules that a later entry adds to the table never a second one and that `Command`/`Call`/`ArgValue` print ids under `Debug` so nothing fields them. The new answer field joins this table's result fields (contract/driver-session/command-schema, decision/refusal-causes-closed-at-eight).

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — `Session::run` the one entry, `validate` first, `Outcome` per verb, rules: nothing public runs an unvalidated `Command`, nothing resolved outlives a call, nothing fields an `Outcome`. The panic catch belongs on this run path (decision/validated-commands-only), and the new field rides `Outcome` under these rules.

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** (socket carries a call and its answer; Driver session contract wire v2 / written forms; nine verbs) — the socket's crossing ratified as a boundary widening with «the next surface that carries them asks again», `Outcome::to_json` / `Refusal::to_json` / `SessionError::to_json` hand-written, `SessionError` with `AnswerTooLarge` (the call ran, oversize), the command line's four endings; «the crate prints nothing» narrowed to its answer line. Matters: the new field must ride these hand-written forms and bounds (decision/hand-written-answers, contract/session-wire/*, contract/session-errors/answer-too-large) and no new session error or exit is admitted.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — the MCP role and its crossing ratified; `serde_json` a reader only; the `tool_call` span with `tool` and `ending` only, standing rule «no span field holds what a call supplied or a screen reads». The MCP result and the tool_call span must carry the new field (or not) under these rules (decision/serde-json-reader-only, contract/tool-call-span/*, contract/mcp-server/tool-result).

**2026-10-12-self-description** — `help` / `describe()` written from the tables alone, `FieldKind` and `NODE_FIELDS` with help, the MCP listing's descriptions carrying result fields; the program's fixed `'static` text ratified on the carriers, while «text from a page, a call or a screen … still widens» and `differs` crosses as a closed set under the rule of 2026-10-10. This is the rule the scope cites (closed value set not a widening; authored text is) and the place the new field's help and listing text must come from (decision/fixed-program-text-on-carriers, decision/measured-limits-stated-in-the-tool).

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — precedent of adding answer content across every carrier: a new `FieldKind`, an `Outcome` variant, the MCP image block, the result bound by whole written form, the `command` span keeping its eight fields and never fielding the image (decision/screenshot-in-band). Same pattern for an errors field.

**2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock** (Driver session and CLIs; ratified by 2026-10-18-engine-debts) — `advance` runs the app's own time step inside one settled step on every session and `Cause` closed at eight; `advance` is one of the five acting verbs whose step can run app code (a handler or task panic), and no cause is admitted for it.

**2026-10-19-session-recording** (the kept check; wire v3, fifteen session errors) — a kept check keeps each answered call owner-only at rest, never logged, with a 64-bit digest; `RecordingFailed`, `ok v3 recording-failed`, `SESSION_ERRORS: [ErrorSpec; 15]`. Matters: the new field rides the kept check and the digest (the P4 design point whether it is held out of the digest), and no session error may be added (decision/recorded-session-checks, contract/kept-check/*).

**2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay** — each kept answer held whole as the driver wrote it, `Check::replay` stopping at the first step whose acceptance or answer differs, a `Change` naming differing result fields in table order; same-host limit for byte-identity. An errors field joining the answer changes replay equality and the committed Counter checks (decision/kept-check-replays-through-run, contract/check-replay/*, decision/committed-stand-checks).

**2026-10-20-load-wait** — the acting step settles through `settle_waiting` on every carrier, with no print or `tracing` call; `snapshot` and `screenshot` wait on nothing. The capture window of «records emitted during the step» is this settled step, and it must stay log-free (contract/load-wait/*).

**2026-10-19-visual-lint** (the gated part: `lint` the twelfth verb) — precedent for a new answer content on every carrier and recorded: closed defect words and numbers, an accepted call recording `verb` alone, findings never fielded, no new carrier, exit, cause or span field (contract/lint-verb/wire-form).

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (the MountedData hazard of a spawned task) — measured that a task spawned from a key handler panicked (`RefCell already borrowed`) inside `render_immediate`; the first recorded handler-path panic, the kind of panic this chunk must catch on the run path.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** (hazard re-measured; component through public API; listener attributes over-report) — a node's owning component reads through Dioxus 0.7.10 public API; hook-local state unreachable; the bridge's listener mark over-reports, the vdom walk reading current listeners exactly. The agent-run harness events (run.start, boot, test, status, cleanup, run.end) and its raw output and log rules. The chunk adds no harness event.

The page script error surface: window error event fields, window.onerror arguments, script error source labels, the embedder drain of script diagnostics, and WPT report messages. These cover page JavaScript, not Dioxus handlers.
Engine document loading rules: a failed stylesheet and the pending critical set, and file loads from non-file documents.
The WASM console panic hook. The chunk reaches the native session only.

Form control and snapshot content rows: select chosen set and list labels, optgroup labels, multiple select form entries, page change events on checkboxes and radios, open list row bounds and shots, and snapshot clickable rows.
CI platform and artifact rows: package-install diagnostic lines, per-leg log and coverage artifacts, and upstream WPT publishing.
The coverage role's line and its shape, owner and logging. The chunk adds nothing to the handler coverage line.

**2026-10-06-telemetry-bootstrap** — wired escher's own stderr sink: engine targets print seven safe fields, `url` · `href` · `src` · `html` · `text` · `value` · `attrs` · `path` · `request` · `error` · `panic.payload` redacted; its reach is that sink only, the std panic hook's raw message staying as-is. This is the scrub the chunk must hold unchanged, and the raw panic-hook message is the known leak beside it: a caught handler panic's payload taken into an answer is authored text on a carrier (the founder's fork), never a reason to loosen `panic.payload`'s redaction.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** (what a sink-installing host logs) — recorded that third-party records (Stylo, dioxus_core) printed ids and names at `debug`/`trace` on the session host, and set the trap: a "nothing in the logs" check over a process that installs no sink passes vacuously. Any proof that the new answer content reaches no log must run against a sink-installing host (`host_log`, `mcp_log`), not an in-process session alone.

**2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist** — made the sink three-outcome: engine targets safe fields only, `escher_` targets with content-named fields redacted, any other target dropped whole at every level, WARN and ERROR included, a bridged record judged by its target. The named cost is that a third-party WARN or ERROR no longer prints. That bears directly on capture: an app handler's own log record (an app target) and most error-level records are dropped by the sink today, so a per-step capture layer must sit beside the sink without changing what it prints (`decision/outside-target-dropped`, `decision/other-log-targets-dropped`, `decision/telemetry-sink-target-allowlist`).

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — built `validate` over a closed verb table and the `Refusal` as a closed set of causes with fixed texts, no `String` field and a `Fault` carrying only the schema's argument name, with no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` on call input. Its rules for later chunks: keep every refusal text fixed and free of call content, and add no cause outside the set. A caught handler panic must not become a new free-text refusal (`decision/closed-refusal-cause-set`, `decision/refusal-holds-no-call-input`, `decision/no-panic-on-call-input`).

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — `Session::run` executes the schema in process, validating first, so nothing public runs a `Command` that did not come from `validate`; an id is looked up anew each call; no panic path on call-supplied input. The acting run path this chunk wraps for panic capture is this one (`decision/one-validation-path-for-every-carrier`, `decision/id-lookup-anew-each-call`), and a caught panic must leave that single path intact.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** — defined the one INFO `command` span per call under `escher_driver` with eight fixed-word or count fields, never an argument, outcome, refusal text or screen content. It also made the sink print closed spans as a second record class (later ratified). Scope's "scrub held": the `command` span gains no field for what an answer now carries (`decision/one-command-span-per-call`, `decision/command-span-content-free`, `contract/driver-command-span/*`).

**2026-10-09-founder-rulings** — ratified the sink's closed-span line and that a diff's three sizes may reach a log while no node, id, name or value of it may. The standing rule: a log field holding any content is a new crossing question. A count of captured errors on the span would itself be a new log field to weigh (`decision/diff-counts-only-in-logs`, `decision/closed-span-lines`).

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** — widened the session socket to carry calls and answers (ids, names, masked values, snapshot text, diff; no `NodeId`). It also made the command line an external surface whose endings echo nothing typed, and gave refusals and session errors written forms from fixed tables. These are the ratified carriers and the no-echo rule the new answer field rides (`decision/session-socket-carries-calls`, `decision/cli-echoes-nothing-typed`, `decision/session-error-fixed-table`, `contract/cli-exit-codes/*`).

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** — the founder's rule: a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is no widening, while a field holding authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still is. This is the rule the scope invokes. Error kinds, node ids and handler event names fit inside it; a panic payload, a log message or a log field's value does not and goes to the founder (`decision/boundary-widening-rule`, `decision/closed-value-field-no-widening`).

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — ratified the MCP stdio crossing (bounded lines and results, fixed protocol errors with no data, refusals as `isError` results) and the `tool_call` span (`tool`, `ending` only) parenting `command`. The new field must appear in MCP tool results and, per the scope, leave the `tool_call` span unchanged (`decision/mcp-result-crossing`, `decision/mcp-bounded-lines`, `contract/mcp-tool-call-span/*`, `contract/mcp-tool-result/is-error`).

**2026-10-12-self-description** — `help` and the MCP listing became the program's own fixed `'static` table text crossing on ratified carriers, ratified with the playbook rule that text from a page, a call or a screen, a new carrier or exit still widens. Session errors became one fixed table with remedies. The new field's `help` and listing text must be fixed table text (`decision/mcp-listing-fixed-text`, `decision/session-errors-fixed-table`).

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — the precedent for open content onto every carrier: pixels are no closed value set, so the in-band image was a boundary widening the founder ratified himself. It added a cause, `fonts-unavailable`, later retired. The rows say the image, its size and dimensions are never fielded. A panic or log text in an answer is the same class: open authored content needing the founder's own word (`decision/screenshot-in-band`).

**2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock** — retired `time-unavailable` and closed the cause set at eight, ratified. A caught panic must not reopen it with a new cause unless the plan names one, which the scope also requires (`decision/closed-refusal-cause-set`).

**2026-10-19-session-recording** — kept checks at rest: owner-only `0700`/`0600` medium, bounds of 400 records and 1,048,576 bytes ending the recording `recording-failed`, the strict `Check::from_bytes` reader, and masked `type` kept as `MASKED_STAND_IN`. The new answer field joins what a kept check holds at rest and its bound (`decision/recording-directory-owner-only`, `decision/recording-bounds-end-recording`, `decision/recorded-check-strict-reader`, `decision/recorded-type-masked`).

**2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay** — a kept check keeps each answer whole as the driver wrote it, with a digest. Replay runs each step through `Session::run` and stops on a differing answer. This is the design point the scope leaves to P4: whether the error field enters the digest. A non-deterministic payload in the digest would make replay stop (`decision/kept-check-answer-whole`, `decision/replay-through-session-run`, `contract/recorded-check/digest`, `contract/recorded-check/answer`).

**2026-10-19-visual-lint** (the gated part) — the precedent for new answer content riding every carrier: `lint`'s findings (ids, closed defect words, numbers) crossed on the socket, command line, MCP and a kept check, ratified. The findings and their count are never fielded on the span, and `host_log`/`mcp_log` drive the verb with 0 needles. The same proof shape applies to the error field.

**2026-10-20-load-wait** — the acting step (`click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll`, on every carrier) settles again within `LOAD_WAIT`, the session reading the wall clock for that wait alone, with no wait argument or result field. This is the settled step whose run the chunk captures errors over. Any capture window must not add a wait field or a new clock read beyond those registered (`decision/load-wait-bound`, `decision/no-wait-verb-fields`, `decision/driver-installs-no-subscriber`).

**2026-10-24-stand-requirement-sweep** — made `host_log` a standing check at `RUST_LOG=trace` over a recording host, with sentinel, id, name and recorded needles at 0 under both builds. This is the check the new answer content's log silence must extend.

**2026-10-25-capability-statement** — reconciled the carried sets at every site (socket, MCP, command line, kept check at rest) and added the committed statement `docs/capabilities.md` of what an MCP client carries onward. A new answer field must be named in every carried-set site and in the statement, or the sets go stale (`decision/capability-statement-mcp-crossing`).

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (the `MountedData` panic from a spawned task) — first recorded that an app's task can panic `RefCell already borrowed` inside the render. This is a measured handler/task panic class the chunk's catch on the run path meets.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** (where a failed load's error text stops) — a failed load's error text stops in `ResourceLoadResponse` and the `Resource load failed` line, where the sink prints the message `[redacted]`, `url` and `error` in its scrub set, and no carrier takes it. An error-level record's text entering an answer would be the first carrier for it: a widening for the founder (`contract/resource-load-failure-log/*`, `contract/network-tracing-log/error`).

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** (the MountedData hazard re-measured and pinned) — pinned the spawned-task panic with `should_panic` tests in both layout modes, its mechanism `poll` holding the document borrow across `render_immediate`. This is history of how an app panic on the run path was measured.

**2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** — removed that panic by rendering into a buffer before borrowing, with a known limit for a task polled during render. The recorder holds no log site and no panic path. Catching a handler panic around `Session::run` must not unwind with the document borrowed or regress this (`decision/dioxus-render-into-buffer`, `decision/try-doc-none-while-borrowed`).

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** — ratified the graph answer crossing (ids, owner ids, component, state and handler event names, closed flag words, booleans; never a value, typed text or `NodeId`) on every carrier including kept checks. It also added the Dioxus bridge dispatch around `runtime.handle_event` with the `SignalRegistry`, inert without a registry, with no log site. The graph's handler identity (owner id, event name) is what the error field ties to, and the dispatch is where handler capture would hook (`decision/graph-answer-crossing`, `decision/dispatch-recorded-only-with-signal-registry`, `decision/signal-registry-holds-no-state-value`, `contract/graph-answer/nodes-states`).

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** — the latest precedent for a ratified widening of answer content onto every carrier (`actions`). Its kept-step replay was left unmeasured and owed as a CARRY. The verb's log silence is proven by 0 needles. Treat the error field's kept-check replay as an owed proof, not an afterthought (`decision/kept-check-actions-answer`).

**2026-11-08-handler-coverage** — added the reached record, written in `handle_event` before dispatch with each reached handler's stable id and event, deduplicated, surviving element removal, with no log site and no `NodeId`. It also added the coverage role reading kept checks as untrusted. The reached record is one candidate attribution mechanism the scope names (`decision/reached-handler-record-without-log`, `decision/reached-record-deduplicated-survives-removal`, `decision/coverage-check-files-untrusted`).

**2026-11-15T05-21-42-wrap** — ratified the coverage role and its line's content and log silence on the founder's own word, replacing the delegate's PROVISIONAL. This confirms that the ratification of a carrier's content is the founder's alone.

**2026-11-14-start-in-a-state** — added `decision/reach-error-closed-set`: reach errors as a closed set with fixed texts holding nothing supplied. The scope says `Session::reach` keeps its contract, and this is the precedent for any error type the chunk adds.

**2026-11-14-auto-exploration** — added `decision/exploration-report-closed-content`: an exploration's report holds closed endings, never a panic payload, `NodeId`, screen text or digest, and is never logged. The scope forbids widening `explore`'s per-path panic ending to carry a payload. It also moved the kept check's opening record to `format: 1`: a changed answer shape in kept checks may bear on the format.

**2026-11-16-layout-explained** — added `decision/session-layout-read-in-process` and widened `decision/no-screen-content-in-logs` to "no driver call or in-process read", the layout answer included. The scope says the layout read keeps its contract. The new answer content must join that row's list of answers kept out of logs.

An acting driver call (click, type, press, advance, scroll) whose step causes a handler panic, an error-level log record or a handler's own log record returns it in that call's answer, beside the diff, each item tied to the stable element id acted on and, through the UI graph, to the handler (owner id and event name).
A handler panic during a step on a held session is caught on the run path and returned as the call's outcome instead of ending the host process.
The records a step causes are captured bounded per call and attributed to the step's target and handler, without changing what the telemetry sink prints.
The new answer field rides every ratified carrier of the acting verbs (in process, session socket call, command line, MCP, kept check recorded and replayed), and the driver's help and MCP tool listing describe it.

body: The acting verbs' answer gains a field carrying the panic, error-level log record or handler log record a step caused, beside the diff; each item is tied to the stable element id the step acted on and to the handler through the UI graph's existing node identity, never a NodeId, and no process-local handle crosses with an id.

A handler panic during a step on a held session is caught on the run path and returned as the call's outcome rather than ending the host process; the driver itself still has no panic path on a call's arguments, and the panic caught is the app handler's.

The capture of a step's records: bounded per call, attributed to the step's target and handler, built through the tracing subscriber, the reached-handler record or the Dioxus handler result; the driver installs no subscriber and reads no environment beyond RUST_LOG, and the reached record stays without log or NodeId.

The boundary widening rule: any authored text (a panic payload, a log message, a log field's value) crossing onto a carrier is a widening and the founder's fork; a new field of a closed value set inside a ratified carrier is no widening; the ratified exits of the stable id, accessible names and attribute text bound what may cross.
The founder's log rulings bound the field: content-free log fields, screen content kept out of logs, one sink line per closed span, and the scrub sets of escher-telemetry.

Scrub held: the telemetry sink's target allowlist, its dropping of outside targets and its redaction of content-named fields (url, href, src, html, text, value, attrs, path, request, error) on escher_ targets stay as they are; the sink prints nothing new.

The driver command span and the MCP tool_call span gain no field holding what the answer now carries; no log line carries the new answer content; driver outcomes are never logged and stable ids and accessible names stay out of logs.
The session socket's call reply (ok v3 accepted and refused forms) carries the new field within its closed grammar, its request-line and oversize bounds.
The command line's result line carries the new field within the driver command line's answer bounds; session output holds no caller input and echoes nothing typed.

The MCP acting tools' results carry the new field within the tool result size bound, with isError and fixed protocol errors as they stand; the MCP listing stays fixed program text that describes the field.

The kept check: the recorded acting answer and its replay through the session hold the new field as the kept check's contents, digest and strict untrusted reader admit; kept checks stay owner-only and the recording directory never named.
The value mask holds on every carrier: a password or file input value never reaches the new field through a captured record or panic payload.

No new carrier, listener, socket, port, verb, exit status or session error; a new refusal cause or result field only as the closed refusal cause set, the fixed session error table and the closed verb schema admit, with refusals holding nothing a call supplied and one validation path for every carrier.

The layout read, explore and Session::reach keep their contracts; explore's per-path panic ending is not widened to carry a payload (exploration report holds closed content only), and reach errors stay a closed set with fixed texts.
The acting verbs' answer stays unpaged and acting commands stay bounded by the load wait; settling and the virtual clock are as they are.
The proof: a minimal fixture app beside the seven_guis stand whose handlers panic, return an error and log, and a new blitz-tests target exercising the field on each carrier in both layout modes.

**2026-10-06-telemetry-bootstrap** — the stand log line and escher-telemetry's scrub tests, with `telemetry_panic_hook` among the one-process-per-behaviour files: the chaining panic hook and the scrub this chunk must hold unchanged while catching a handler panic on the run path already have checks of their own.

**2026-10-06-stand-test-contract** — the agent-run five-command contract (selections `stand` · `all` · `{name}`, events carrying no captured test output). A new non-`stand_` target is reached by `run all` / `run {name}` alone, and no panic text may reach an event.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** (trap) — a deleting key press is not the same on every platform (the Backspace arm is compiled out on macOS). Any key the fixture's panicking or logging handler is driven by must read the same on every CI OS.

**2026-10-07-audit-corrections** — the bridge tests sit in a `cfg(test)` child module with no constructor or `pub` widened; `tests/blitz-tests` keeps one target per behaviour beside shared modules that are no target. These are the origins of the `bridge-tests-without-widening` and `one-test-target-per-behaviour` rows. A test of handler attribution in the bridge must keep both.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — opens the Session lifecycle key and the process-check rules. Traps: an `#[ignore]` host child blocks a bare `--ignored` run; a child's inherited libtest lines are counted as tests; a sink-installing host at `trace` overruns an undrained pipe. A panicking handler on a host process meets all three.

**2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist** — `host_log` covers a sink-installing host at `trace` with needles read from the stand, and `telemetry_drop` proves third-party targets dropped. Traps: a check that must fail red on a leaking sink cannot use `start` on a piped host; a needle list read from the stand can outgrow a hand-kept one. This is the template for proving no log line carries the new answer content.

**2026-10-07-settle-detection** — `Session::act` returns settled or `NotSettled(Busy)` with the instance still readable, not rolled back; settle neither advances time nor drains the changed set. A caught handler panic must fit this outcome model (the step not rolled back). The changed set is non-empty on a fresh harness, so drain it first.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — the schema's pins: every table stated in its test with its row count asserted, an assertion over a call carrying a row index only, and each pin under a mutation control. A new result field enters only as the schema tables admit, and its pins follow the row-index-only rule.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — the `stand_act_*` files drive `Session::run` in both layout modes. Rule set: a driver check's failure message names a layout mode, a task and an index, never an id or what a screen reads. The new behaviour's checks inherit it.

**2026-10-07-refusal-detection** — refusal order `disabled` · `off-screen` · `covered`, `stale` / `not-found` lookup, and refused calls leaving the instance unchanged. A refused acting call runs no handler, so it must carry no caused error.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** — `stand_act_spans`: one `command` span line per call, fixed words and counts only, with typed text measured at 0 in process. Traps: a check reading a sink's capture counts lines by target, never in total; a green per-package run is not the workspace leg's green, because engine `tracing` is on in the workspace build only. Under the scrub-held boundary, the span gains no field.

**2026-10-09-founder-rulings** — the closed-span second record class in the stand log was ratified by the founder (the origin of the `closed-spans-logged-as-lines` row). This is one of the log rulings that bound what of a log may enter an answer.

**2026-10-10-upstream-sync-agent-surfaces** — `BlitzTestsTargetsTest` pins one auto-discovered target per file, with upstream's `all` held at `test = false`. The new target needs no manifest line, and none may be added.

A handler panic during an acting step on a held session is caught on the run path and returned as the call's outcome instead of ending the host process; what the instance is after a caught panic (poisoned, rebooted or held) is a behaviour the chunk sets and its checks must state.
The acting verbs as a set — click, type, press, advance, scroll — and their run validation and settle: each carries the new field, and the field is empty where the step caused nothing.

The capture of a step's records is bounded per call; the answer stays within the session wire's answer bound, and an over-bound answer meets the existing oversize and answer-too-large handling, never a new error.
The UI graph's handler identity (owner key id form, owner id and event name) and the reached record are what tie an item to its handler; no raw node handle enters an answer.

Run carriers: the session socket's call and its graph and acting answers, the command line's actions verb and its output, the MCP role's tool results and the in-process run all carry the same new field with the same content.

The driver's help and the MCP tools/list describe the new field, and the help on the command line and over MCP stay at parity; the capability statement pinned to the driver schema is held to the schema's new field.

The kept check: the session recording's record fields and replay through the ordinary call path carry the new field (or hold it out of the digest, a P4 point), and committed recorded checks stay byte-equal to the binary's recording and kept fresh.
Scrub held: the telemetry target allowlist and scrub of named fields stay as they are, and a step's capture changes nothing of what the sink prints; the sink still drops third-party targets.

No log line carries the new answer content: the driver's command span and the tool_call span gain no field, the driver's per-call log line keeps fixed words and counts only, and host stderr carries no screen content at any level.

Answers and logs hold no value: an actions or graph answer holds no typed value and a typed password is never returned; any authored text (panic payload, log message, a log field's value) entering an answer is the founder's boundary fork, bounded by his content-free log rulings.

No new carrier, listener, socket, verb, exit status or session error: the refusal causes, their order, the session error set and the exit statuses stay closed; a new refusal cause or result field enters only as the schema tables admit.
No panic path on a driver call's arguments: a refused call changes nothing and echoes no input; a panic caught is the app handler's, never the driver's.
Exploration keeps its contract: its per-path panic ending carries no payload, and exploration checks in the recording are not widened; the layout read and Session::reach keep theirs.

Test failures and agent-run output print no argument value and no panic text: the new tests' assertions must not print the captured payloads they compare.
